# Pyreto

> Python port of Ulrich Riegel's R package "Pareto": Pareto, piecewise Pareto and generalized Pareto distributions for reinsurance (excess-of-loss) pricing. Fit collective models to layer losses, excess frequencies or PML curves, then price layers, compute variances and simulate annual losses.

Install from GitHub, not PyPI (the PyPI "pyreto" is a different package): `pip install "pyreto @ git+https://github.com/o1iv3r/Pyreto"`. Fitting functions signal failure through `model.status == 2` and `model.comment`, not exceptions.

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/agents/): workflows, failure handling and conventions for coding agents
- [Vignette](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/vignette/): worked examples
- [Function mapping](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/function_mapping/): R name to Python name

## API reference

- [Models and collective-model functions](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/api/models/): PPPModel, PGPModel, layer_mean, layer_var, layer_sd, excess_frequency, simulate_losses
- [Fitting](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/api/fitting/): fit_references, piecewise_pareto_match_layer_losses, fit_pml_curve, local_pareto_alpha
- [Pareto](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/api/pareto/): layer moments, alpha finders, extrapolation
- [Piecewise Pareto](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/api/piecewise_pareto/)
- [Generalized Pareto](https://o1iv3r.github.io/Pyreto/api/gen_pareto/)
